messages:
alex: quick notes from today's GPTQ bakebot run across Llama/Mistral/Qwen. short version: Mistral-7B-gptq shows KV-cache degradation on long-context evals, qwen-7b-int8 has a small but consistent numeric-answer delta, llama-2-13b-gptq fine but higher tail latency under batching.

bakebot: automated-run: job=gbx-2026-03-20-03, models=[mistral-7b-gptq,qwen-7b-int8,llama-2-13b-gptq], evalsets=[long-context,mathbench,mt-quality], samples=1200, seed=42, artifacts=/s3/bake/gbx-3135792468/

sophie: can you paste the minimal repro for the mistral kv issue?

alex: gist of repro (ran on a single 80k-seq synthetic session):
```
# run with our bake script
python bakebot/run_bake.py --model mistral-7b-gptq --quant gptq --max-length 65536 --eval long-context --seed 42 --out /tmp/mistral-kv-drop.json
```
observed: first 4k tokens match baseline, after ~4k there's token divergence and KV cache hit rate drops ~30%.

matt: interesting. did you compare with kernel-level KV flushing? sometimes miscompiled kernels behave weird on Mistral attention patterns.

alex: yup — recompiled with kernel v2.1 and v2.3. v2.1 produced the drop; v2.3 fixes it in most runs. patching kernel selection in runtime avoided the worst regressions.

rachel: eval snapshot (summary):
- mistral-7b-gptq: long-context exact-match delta vs fp16: -6.2% on long-context QA, BLEU stable for short hops
- qwen-7b-int8: mathbench numeric accuracy delta: -3.1%, language exact-match delta: -0.6%
- llama-2-13b-gptq: mathbench delta: -0.4%, tail-p99 latency +12ms under batch size 8

sophie: do we have any examples showing the KV hit-rate drop? even 1-2 short transcripts would help.

alex: pasted one short trace below (token-level truncated):
"prompt: <long doc> ..."
"fp16 continuation: ... 42 is the answer"
"gptq continuation (post-4k): ... 7 is the answer"
metrics: kv_hits_before=98%, kv_hits_after=67%

ignacio: my hunch: Mistral kv layout + GPTQ pointer offsets misaligned for certain block sizes. can we try a non-contiguous KV layout experiment? set runtime flag --kv-layout=segmented to force block-aligned caches.

alex: tried segmented and observed kv_hits_after ~84% (much better); cost per-token up ~2% but latency more stable.

matt: for qwen numeric delta — was that consistent across seeds? sometimes AWQ/int8 variants have slight bias on floating softmax tails.

rachel: checked seeds 42/7/13: qwen-7b-int8: -3.1, -2.9, -3.4 — consistent. error modes: off-by-one on arithmetic and occasional formatted-output hallucinations.

sophie: any deployment profile recs?

ignacio: proposal: for Mistral-7B-gptq use profile "mistral-stable-v2":
- kernel-selection: prefer v2.3
- kv-layout: segmented
- batch-target: 6 (avoid p99 spikes)
- prefetch-window: 512 tokens

alex: and for Qwen-7B-int8: prefer AWQ fallback for mathbench-heavy workloads or keep int8 but enable "numeric-calibration" post-quant step (calib-set = mathbench-like).

ops-bot: CI entry created: #ci/3135792468-add-mistral-stable-v2-profile (cherry-pick to staging).

matt: follow-ups: run longer-run stability (24h synthetic) with segmented KV and kernel v2.3; instrument per-layer kv validity counters.

rachel: i'll prepare a short eval excel with the per-task deltas and attach to the bake artifacts. quick note: these changes would raise cost ~1.8% but cut p99 errors by ~60%.

sophie: thanks — this is actionable. tagging eng-runtime to expedite kernel promotion. :eyes:

alex: thanks all. i'll capture these as the bakebot fieldnotes and add an ops playbook snippet for mistral kv regressions.

bakebot: artifacts uploaded: /s3/bake/gbx-3135792468/logs.tar.gz, /s3/bake/gbx-3135792468/eval_snapshot.json

ops-bot: slack-thread-closed: reason=summary-posted, followups=[#ci/3135792468-add-mistral-stable-v2-profile]
